rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the probability or possibility of harm, including a person or thing that poses a risk.

example.english: There is a risk in joining this plan.
example.jyutping: caam1 gaa1 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 jau5 fung1 him2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for doing something despite a known danger.

example.english: Going swimming in such heavy rain is really a risk.
example.traditional: 落咁大雨仲去游水，真係冒險喎。
example.jyutping: lok6 gam3 daai6 jyu5 zung6 heoi3 jau4 seoi2 zan1 hai6 mou6 him2 wo3

rows.note: Use this construction when an action or situation puts a person or thing in danger.

example.english: Walking this mountain path alone at night can put you in danger—you risk getting hurt.
example.traditional: 夜晚一個人行呢條山路，會令你有危險。
example.jyutping: je6 maan5 jat1 go3 jan4 haang4 ni1 tiu4 saan1 lou6 wui5 ling6 nei5 jau5 ngai4 him2

rows.note: Use this for an imminent or concrete danger rather than an abstract assessment of probability.

example.english: The wet road ahead poses a risk, so walk slowly.
example.traditional: 前面條路濕滑，好危險，行慢啲。
example.jyutping: cin4 min6 tiu4 lou6 sap1 waat6 hou2 ngai4 him2 haang4 maan6 di1

rows.note: Use this when the person or thing is viewed as an active threat to someone or something.

example.english: This virus is a risk to the elderly.
example.traditional: 呢個病毒對長者嚟講係一種威脅。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 beng6 duk6 deoi3 coeng4 ze2 lei4 gong2 hai6 jat1 zung2 wai1 hip3
